clue.text: Short of a penny, cleaned bike

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so one letter is dropped from the word for cleaned

parts.note: to clean a floor is to mop it, past tense mopped
P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: Someone a penny short of the fare gave their bike a wash instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a small motorised bicycle, a light motorbike with pedals.

clue.text: Conductor expressing Mahler's Sixth well and with dignity

indicators.note: to express is to squeeze out, so the letter is pressed out of the word for conductor

parts.note: a maestro is an eminent conductor

indicators.note: the sixth letter of the name is taken, punning on Mahler's Sixth Symphony

parts.note: so, as in 'so, what now?', can stand for well

explanation.surface: A conductor performing Mahler's Sixth Symphony both well and with grandeur.
explanation.walkthrough: The sixth letter of MAHLER is R; 'expressing' squeezes it out of MAESTRO, leaving MAESTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestoso is an Italian musical direction meaning to be played in a stately, majestic manner.

clue.text: Metal from a can containing fruit? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece containing another holds it inside
on the contrary reverses the stated relation, so the fruit holds the can rather than the can the fruit

parts.note: a plum is a stone fruit
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Metal from a tin of fruit, though it turns out the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a precious silvery-white metallic element.

clue.text: In play, one posh actor needs to speak like Cockney

indicators.note: in play suggests the letters are played about with, moving freely

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A well-spoken actor must learn a Cockney accent for a stage role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is I, not the letters O N E. A Cockney is a working-class Londoner whose accent leaves off the h sound at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitting the h sound, saying 'ouse' for house, is the stereotypical mark of a Cockney accent.

clue.text: What Sandra will do to make Sara abandon hope?

definitions.text: What Sandra will do to make Sara
definitions.meaning: taking the middle two letters N and D out of the name Sandra leaves Sara, so Sandra must lose her centre
to give up hope or become discouraged

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about what one woman must do to become another, ending in despair.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of SANDRA is its middle pair ND; drop them and SARA is left, so the cryptic reading is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: To become discouraged and give up is the idiomatic sense of losing courage or spirit.

clue.text: Direct current is supplied by it

definitions.meaning: to direct is to guide or be in charge of
an electrical wire or flex carries current to an appliance

explanation.surface: Direct current, as in electricity, comes from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct current' reads as one electrical phrase; split it after 'Direct'.
explanation.definitionFit: To guide is to head the way; an electric cable connecting a device carries the current.

clue.text: Set adrift, Papa married different person — her?

definitions.text: Set adrift, Papa married different person — her?

indicators.note: something adrift is loose and out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is Papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an other is a different person from oneself

explanation.surface: Cut loose, Dad wed someone else: is she the one?
explanation.walkthrough: 'adrift' rearranges SET into STE. Read whole, the clue describes a father who has moved on and remarried.
explanation.definitionFit: A father's new wife is the replacement mother figure for his children.

clue.text: Error in the copy Charlie edited is "between you and I" perhaps

indicators.note: copy that has been edited is rearranged and reworked

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sub-editor's lament about a grammatical slip in Charlie's article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Error' looks like the definition but is fodder. Speakers who think 'me' is wrong say 'between you and I', overcorrecting.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcorrecting by applying a grammar rule where it does not belong produces this slip; the phrase is an example.

clue.text: Charge added to bill for buttonhole

indicators.note: the word for charge is added to the end of the bill

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a cost is a charge or price

explanation.surface: An extra fee tacked on to an invoice for a flower in a lapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buttonhole' looks like a lapel flower; here it is a verb, to waylay someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttonhole someone is to detain them in talk, approaching boldly.

clue.text: Officer has no place for resident

indicators.note: having no part means it is missing, so that part is removed

parts.note: a lieutenant is a junior army or navy officer
lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'

explanation.surface: An officer with nowhere to live is looking for somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone occupying rented property lives there as an occupant.

clue.text: Cast are able to add more detail

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, and thrown letters land in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Actors in the cast are able to flesh out their parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the theatrical company but is the anagram signal for ARE ABLE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate on something is to expand it, filling in further particulars.

clue.text: Exercise extremes of caution eating a nut

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: one piece eating another holds it inside, so the A goes within the outer letters
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Advice to take care while snacking on a nut, perhaps over an allergy.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is a smooth-shelled nut from a North American hickory tree.

clue.text: Stand to succeed finally after lapse

indicators.note: the final letters come after the word for lapse, so they follow it

parts.note: a trip is a slip or stumble, a lapse

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Advice to stand firm and come out on top after a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged support for a camera or telescope is a kind of stand.

clue.text: Lock up rogue, no gentleman on reflection

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal

indicators.note: a reflection shows a thing back to front, so the following words are read backwards

parts.note: sir is the address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A decision, after thinking it over, to jail a villain who is no gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns NO SIR into RISON.
explanation.definitionFit: To jail someone is to confine them behind bars.

clue.text: A fact: worked equal shifts to make bier

indicators.note: worked suggests the letters are kneaded into a new order
shifts says these letters move about into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A fact: shift workers on equal hours build a coffin stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges A FACT into CATAF and 'shifts' rearranges EQUAL into ALQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform on which a coffin lies in state is a decorated stand for a body.

clue.text: Lack of sense sets back European political group

indicators.note: back says the word for sets is read in reverse

parts.note: to set something down is to put it, so sets gives puts
a faction is a dissenting group within a party

explanation.surface: A sneer that a European party is setting back common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A dazed state of astonishment leaves one unable to think, a temporary loss of the senses.

clue.text: Male wants females, we're told, to intimidate

parts.note: a bull is a male of cattle, elephants, whales and more

indicators.note: we're told means heard rather than read, so the sound of the word is entered

parts.note: does are female deer or rabbits

explanation.surface: A man after women is told to throw his weight about.
explanation.definitionFit: To bulldoze someone is to force or bully them into something.

clue.text: First to last, rabble-rousing publications

indicators.note: the first letter is moved to the last position, from the front of the word to its end

parts.note: stirring up a mob against authority is sedition

explanation.surface: Inflammatory pamphlets from first page to last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First to last' moves S of SEDITION to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Printings of a book or newspaper are issues, each a version brought out at one time.

clue.text: Place for soldiers that could provide a padre?

parts.note: the letters of a padre can come from a six-letter word for a march past, crushed into a new order; the second answer word is that crushing signal

explanation.surface: A place where soldiers drill that might yield an army chaplain.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: GROUND, meaning crushed, is an anagram signal acting on PARADE, which gives A PADRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops drill and are inspected on a large open space at a barracks.

clue.text: Jack is after small vehicle — a Beetle

indicators.note: the sailor comes after, so follows the small vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a jack tar is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

explanation.surface: Jack wants a small car, a VW Beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beetle is the Volkswagen car, but here it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Every year, a chap flips lid

parts.note: PA is per annum, Latin for each year

indicators.note: flips says the following words are turned over and read in reverse

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Every year some fellow loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flips lid' suggests losing one's temper; lid is slang for hat. 'flips' turns A MAN into NAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lid is slang for a hat, and a Panama is a straw hat.

clue.text: Cobblers give a hand with door

parts.note: to give someone a hand is to applaud them
a trap is a trapdoor, a hinged door in a floor or ceiling

explanation.surface: Shoemakers lending a hand with a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' is British slang for nonsense, not shoemakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobblers is British slang for rubbish talk, empty and pretentious nonsense.

clue.text: Old fool grabs tail of Siamese cat

indicators.note: the word for fool grabs the letter and holds it inside

parts.note: a clot is a stupid person

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An old fool catches a Siamese cat by the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a wild spotted cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Stick around the centre of Geneva

parts.note: CA is circa, around, used with dates

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A direction to stay put in the middle of Geneva.
explanation.definitionFit: A walking stick or rod for punishing is a cane.

clue.text: Attain some rare achievements

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A modest observation about reaching uncommon feats.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain a goal is to arrive at it, to get to it.

clue.text: Bell-ringer, as it were, meeting terrible doom

parts.note: quasi means seemingly, as it were

indicators.note: terrible suggests the word doom is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer meeting a terrible fate, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo's hunchback of Notre-Dame rang the cathedral bells.

clue.text: Comparatively loud English supporter

parts.note: brassy means loud and showy, so more so is brassier

explanation.surface: A louder English fan in the stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' suggests a fan; it is a bra.
explanation.definitionFit: A bra is an undergarment that holds up and supports the bust.

clue.text: Calls for works to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard says the word is said aloud and a word of the same sound is entered

parts.note: to knead dough is to work it with the hands

explanation.surface: A demand for some works to be performed or listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that requires a thing makes it necessary, demanding it.
